doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: Two weeks in San Francisco with Monk and how he got the job
summary: Smith describes hanging out with Monk, refuting the image of him as strange, and how he got the gig when Monk's rhythm section had to return to New York. Monk invites him to Shelly's.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Oh yeah. No I was called to work a week — two weeks in San Francisco. And in the middle of the second week he had — and I hung out with him every minute, I mean, and he wasn’t strange, you know like they always picture him as a weirdo, he’s not weird. Not at all. You know and he’s not effusive. He’d go sometimes a couple of days and not say anything at all, but if you’re not afraid of large black men, you know, all you have to do is be around a few and you realize hey man, like I think that, you know this is my own opinion I think writers, first they form an opinion like oh my God, you know, oh my God, this guy is scary, he’s scary and he’s going to steal my car you know. And then when a writer is, they’re going to pay you $40 to write a review of a performance and you have to go to the gig and buy a drink and, you know you end up like, that a large amount of the writing comes from reading previous reviews. Because it becomes like written in stone that Thelonious is strange. He’s not strange. He’s a little bit shy and also he’s funny as hell. But anyway so I don’t know if it was in the ending of the first week or the middle of the second he said to me, he says, “You want to go to Shelly’s with me?” You know he had gotten a call. The reason I got the gig was because he had done a tour of Asia and Bill Cosby at that time was paying jazz musicians who wanted to become actors, paying their admission, their tuition to Manhattan School of Acting. And so the bass player and the tenor player, I think it was Charlie Rouse and I’m not sure if it was Bob Cranshaw, but it was somebody like that, they had to be back to New York. So Thelonious got this last minute booking in San Francisco and so they were looking for a bass player and I got recommended by several people who knew I knew his stuff. Anyway he said, “Do you want to go to Shelly’s with me?” And my tail is still wagging.
That’s a great way to put it.
